text:
Cambodian rice is grown in four main ecosystems: upland rainfed rice, lowland rainfed rice, deepwater/floating rice, and irrigated (controlled-water) rice.

Planting and harvest timing are matched to variety maturity duration. For varieties with a 120-day growth duration, farmers plant from month 6 to month 9 (June-September) and harvest from month 8 to month 11 (August-November). For varieties with a 121-150 day duration, farmers plant starting in month 7 (July), with flowering occurring between 15 October and 15 November. For varieties with a growth duration longer than 150 days, farmers plant from month 6 to month 7 (June-July) and harvest at the end of month 1 (January); for deepwater rice specifically within this longer-duration group, flowering occurs between 1 November and 15 December.

Note: this entry summarizes rice ecosystems and duration-based planting/harvest windows from one training slide; it may overlap with the existing KB topics 'rice_ecosystem_types' and 'cropping_calendar' but is retained because it ties specific flowering/harvest date windows to three variety-duration classes (120 days, 121-150 days, and >150 days).
